Retrieved 2026-07-19 via Exa full fetch. BBC News (Kate Whannel), published 2026-07-19 11:29 BST. Reports Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg (aired ~09:00 BST Sun 19 July 2026).

- Lucy Powell (Labour deputy leader) on Kuenssberg: Burnham will stand by 2024 manifesto promises but be "bolder and more ambitious"; leadership a moment for "clearing the decks of all the other things that might distract" from cost of living and the economy.
- Powell: "Our manifesto did talk about the redistribution of power, it did talk about the rewiring of our country, it did talk about taking on some of those vested interests." / "He [Burnham] really understands the bigger, bolder measures that are needed to live up to the manifesto promises."
- Powell: scrapping the Digital ID scheme a "small example of reprioritising"; scheme would have cost a "not insignificant amount of money" and diverted attention from priorities.
- Powell on North Sea: Burnham would be "pragmatic"; "I don't think it's a change of policy. It's more a change of emphasis."
- Powell on public ownership: economy had been "overly privatised", "utilities and essentials of life don't work in the interest of ordinary people"; bills "going up and up because they are run in the interests of private interest, not for the consumers or for taxpayers".
- Kemi Badenoch (Con leader) on same programme: Burnham a "people pleaser" at a time the country needed someone who could "take tough decisions, who can face down Labour MPs". "The job is not a popularity contest... he has not said what he's going to do. It's all airy-fairy stuff."
- Jacob Rees-Mogg (former Con minister) on same programme: "The water industry needs private capital or it has to have taxpayers' money - no other money is available."
- Package expected: new North Sea oil/gas drilling; water and energy under public control; new council house-building programme.
